blindSummary:
On 19 July 2026 the government of this state/province's largest city announced it was preparing a local regulation rejecting LGBT, presented as follow-through on a 2025 presidential regulation that lists the "spread of LGBTQ culture" among non-military threats to national defence alongside terrorism and trafficking. The city's mayor made the announcement in the courtyard of a large mosque. This state/province also appears in an international LGBT-rights organisation's set of eight flagged states/provinces with discriminatory regulation. The local regulation remains in preparation, not yet enacted, with no specified penalty or enforcement event documented.

The deviation from the country's average is small and sits below it, similar to a neighbouring state/province. The 2025 presidential-regulation framing elevates local anti-LGBT rules from moral panic to national-defence doctrine - activists say this legitimised a mob attack in a city in another state/province - but without a specific enacted penalty the traveler-facing risk remains prospective. It sits above a neighbouring state/province that has a live local regulation with specified sanctions in two articles, and above the country's floor, where no equivalent regulation has been announced.
